principles.statement: Represent beginner grammar as communicative form–meaning–use constructions rather than isolated rules whenever the representation remains pedagogically accurate.
Capture a meaningful interpretation attempt before using rule-test success as evidence of construction knowledge.

Design structured interpretation tasks so the target grammatical form contributes necessary information to the correct meaning, rather than allowing shortcut answers from unrelated lexical or visual cues.
Use production practice after or alongside form–meaning processing because receptive success and productive availability are distinct and production can add delayed productive gains.
Treat explicit grammar explanation as bounded support: use the smallest explanation that resolves confusion, record its presence, and return immediately to interpretation or use.
Do not make highlighting, bolding or textual enhancement the active learning mechanism; require processing of the highlighted form's meaning or function.

Begin construction learning with a small number of clear, useful exemplars and then vary lexical/contextual slots to test generalization; do not infer a universal exemplar count from frequency theory.
Preserve rule/metalinguistic knowledge, interpretation, controlled production, changed-context production, real-time processing and delayed retention as separate grammar evidence dimensions.
Never infer an 'implicit grammar mastery' percentage from one timed test, elicited-imitation task or grammaticality judgment without a separately validated measurement model.
Keep support provenance for every construction attempt, including model visibility, explanation language, choices, prompts and reformulations.
Use corrective feedback inside meaningful use, but select prompt versus model/reformulation according to learner and error evidence rather than one globally preferred feedback type.

When the learner likely has the target form, a self-repair prompt is a candidate first repair; when the form is unavailable or unstable, provide bounded positive evidence/modeling instead of forcing repeated guessing.
Sequence grammar across listening, reading, speaking and writing around the same construction so progress reflects flexible use rather than success in a dedicated Grammar tab.

Use high-frequency and prototypical exemplars as curriculum candidates, not as automatic mastery or universal teaching-order rules; learner prerequisites and communicative value still govern selection.
Require changed-context and delayed unseen probes before promoting a construction from guided use to independently usable knowledge.
Keep the exact explanation timing, exemplar distribution, interpretation-to-production threshold and feedback policy falsifiable until EXP-012 validates them with Vietnamese near-A0 learners.
